q1-cum-laps.title: What does 'cumulative car-laps' mean as the intra-session evolution index?
q1-cum-laps.imperative: Resolve from code/docs+design spec: is 'cumulative car-laps' (issue #663, DESIGN_SPEC.md S2) the same concept as the existing 'cumulative_track_laps' bridge column already scaffolded on EstimateRecord (estimate_store.py), i.e. the FIELD-total count of laps completed by ALL cars on track up to a point in the session (a rubber-laid-down / track-evolution proxy) -- or a PER-CAR lap count (that car's own laps so far)? The exploration digest (xR5 in DESIGN_SPEC.md) says 'track evolution has no validated public model; index to cumulative car-laps' in the context of TRACK evolution, and the existing bridge column is named cumulative_track_laps and described as 'the W3 track-evolution axis'. Resolve and record code evidence (grep for cumulative_track_laps computation, if any exists yet).
q1-cum-laps.finding: FACT resolved: 'cumulative car-laps' (issue #663 / DESIGN_SPEC S2) IS the existing field-wide cumulative_track_laps concept, NOT a per-car lap count. Authoritative definition already implemented+battle-tested: src/physics/layer2/session_race.py:268 compute_cumulative_track_laps(session_id, first_clean_lap_num, db_path) -> int -- 'Count of (driver, lap) pairs with lap_number < first_clean_lap_num' (ALL cars, regardless of valid_lap/track_status; docstring explicitly: 'total rubber laid down before this stint started'). Used by stint_estimator.py:834/875, damage_batch.py:224, estimate_store.py's cumulative_track_laps bridge column (already scaffolded, populate_cumulative_track_laps_for_demo at line 463), race_stint_store.py:101. session_race.py:360 session_cumulative_track_laps() wraps it at ONE representative (fastest-clean-lap) anchor per (constructor,session) -- G needs the PER-LAP value across many laps within a session to fit the intra-session curve, so G will replicate compute_cumulative_track_laps's exact counting convention (lap_number < X, ALL cars) vectorized as one query per session (cumulative count over sorted lap_number) rather than N per-lap SQL calls -- same definition, different call shape for performance. This closes the #626 layer2_evolution.py Known Limit (which explicitly floated for lack of exactly this bridge) since G will BE that bridge.

q2-session-scope.title: Which session_types does G fit/estimate cover?
q2-session-scope.imperative: tyre_supplant.py's compound/tyre-age/fuel correction machinery (race_degradation_slopes) is built specifically for RACE laps (session_type='R': stints, pit stops, multi-lap degradation regression). Quali sessions (Q/SQ) have too few laps per driver (banker laps) for the same within-session OLS regression. Yet G's inter-session offset must span the whole weekend (FP1-FP3-Q-SQ-R) to absorb overnight/support-series/temperature per the design. DECISION (in Commander latitude -- fit/test decision, not a scope/boundary change): scope G's FIT (curve+offset estimation via the tyre_supplant-style regression) to session types with enough lap volume for the correction (FP1/FP2/FP3/R); Q/SQ sessions fall under the #560 thin-session rule (q3) rather than getting a bespoke quali-specific correction model in this build. This keeps G's Build-1 scope bounded and precedented (reuses tyre_supplant as-is rather than building a parallel quali correction). Record as self-resolved per delegated latitude (fit/test decision); float only if this later proves to have ramifications beyond G.
q2-session-scope.finding: DECISION self-resolved (in-latitude fit/test decision), REVISED from the initial recommendation after checking real 2023 data: G's fit runs UNIFORMLY across ALL session types (FP1/FP2/FP3/Q/SQ/R/S), generalizing tyre_supplant._read_clean_race_laps's hardcoded session_type='R' filter to a parameter -- NOT a blanket per-type exclusion of Q/SQ. Evidence (2023 DB, 22 events): stint-level median laps/stint = FP1:5, FP2:5, FP3:3, Q:2, R:18, SQ:3, S:16; Q sessions are structurally thin (76.8% of driver-stints <4 laps; 17/22 Q sessions have <2 dry compounds present) -- but this is a per-SESSION support property, not an inherent property of the session TYPE that justifies hardcoding an exclusion. The #560 thin-session rule (q3) is the correct mechanism to catch this case-by-case (most Q sessions will fall into wide-sigma fallback, but the mechanism is uniform and reusable rather than a special-cased skip).

q3-thin-rule.title: #560 thin-session rule: what does G do with a session too thin to fit?
q3-thin-rule.imperative: Pre-ruling decision:thin-session-explicit requires an explicit rule (skip / wide-sigma fallback / floor), grounded by inspecting 2023 thin-session incidence, choosing the rule that fails visibly. Inspect the 2023 DB (lap_times/sessions) for per-session per-driver flying-lap counts to characterize incidence before choosing. Record the chosen rule + its rationale + its 2023 incidence count. This is explicitly named in-latitude in the launch order (float only if epic-wide ramifications) -- self-resolve unless the inspection reveals a genuinely epic-wide ramification.
q3-thin-rule.finding: DECISION self-resolved (in-latitude, launch order explicitly names this as mine to choose): rule = WIDE-SIGMA FALLBACK, never silent skip -- reuses the SAME mechanism the design spec already names for the rain-flag case ('rain flag forces offset re-estimation with wide sigma'), extended to structural thinness for mechanism-uniformity. Floor (named constant, reusing tyre_supplant.MIN_STINT_LAPS=4 rather than inventing a new one): a session's within-session curve+offset gets a NORMAL fit only if it has >=2 usable driver-stints with >=MIN_STINT_LAPS(4) laps each; below that floor, the session's offset is estimated via nearest-neighbor extrapolation within the same weekend (adjacent session's fitted curve value at the equivalent cumulative_track_laps position) with an inflated sigma (named factor, frozen before first real-data run per F12 discipline) rather than a NULL/dropped record -- this is the 'fails visibly' choice: a consumer checking sigma(G) sees honestly-large uncertainty instead of a falsely-confident thin fit (the exact #560 complaint: 'thin fits currently pass acceptance with no minimum-flying-laps floor'). 2023 incidence measured directly: stint-level thin(<4 laps) rate = FP1 35.0%, FP2 36.4%, FP3 52.1%, Q 76.8%, R 11.4%, SQ 58.7%, S 2.2% (1421/1257/1168/1940/1286/332/134 total driver-stints respectively). No epic-wide ramification identified (SegmentMap/#661 and other consumers are untouched by this choice) -- not floated.

q4-heldout-split.title: Held-out reconciliation gate: what is the disjoint split axis?
q4-heldout-split.imperative: The GATING acceptance test requires G fit on a SUBSET of drivers/laps, scored on the DISJOINT remainder (not in-sample). Decide the split axis: driver-based split (fit G's per-session curve+offset using a subset of drivers' laps; evaluate cross-session same-driver/compound/similar-fuel reconciliation error using the HELD-OUT drivers only) is the natural choice since G is field-pooled per session across drivers. Verify the 2023 DB has enough drivers-with-multi-session-laps to support a real driver split (not just a synthetic-only gate). Record as self-resolved fit/test decision (in latitude); include the concrete split scheme (e.g. ~50/50 stratified by team, or another scheme) and cite driver-count evidence from the DB.
q4-heldout-split.finding: DECISION self-resolved (in-latitude): driver-based split, ~50/50 stratified by team where team info available (session_classifications.team), else plain random 50/50 with a fixed seed. Evidence: 2023 DB has median 20 drivers/session across ALL session types (min 15-20), comfortably supporting a 10-vs-10 split for a field-pooled per-session curve+offset fit. Held-out gate mechanics: fit G's per-session curve+offset using only the FIT-set drivers' laps (with the tyre_supplant-style correction); then for the HELD-OUT drivers, compute cross-session reconciliation error (same driver, same compound, similar-fuel-state laps in a DIFFERENT session of the same weekend) both with and without subtracting the fit-set-derived G; G passes the gate if subtracting it reduces the held-out reconciliation error (not just in-sample).

q5-synthetic-criterion.title: Synthetic-recovery test: what quantitative criterion counts as 'separable'?
q5-synthetic-criterion.imperative: The GATING synthetic-recovery test requires the fit to recover an injected known curve + known session offsets 'separably' -- curve initial value vs. offset are aliased in principle; if not separable, sigma(G) is structurally understated downstream. Decide a concrete, falsifiable criterion (e.g. recovered curve/offset parameters within N-sigma of injected ground truth across M synthetic replicates with varying noise/session-count, AND the fit's own reported posterior covariance between curve-initial-value and offset stays below some correlation threshold, evidencing the aliasing is resolved rather than papered over by a wide/uninformative posterior). Record as self-resolved fit/test decision (in latitude, precedented pattern -- LOO/synthetic-recovery discipline already used project-wide per lesson:loo-residual-diagnostic-over-self-weighted-predictor).
q5-synthetic-criterion.finding: DECISION self-resolved (in-latitude, precedented LOO/synthetic-recovery pattern project-wide): criterion = (a) PARAMETER RECOVERY -- across >=50 synthetic replicates (varying noise sigma, session count, driver count matched to real 2023 session-shape distributions), the fit's recovered curve-asymptote/rate and each session's recovered offset fall within their own reported 2-sigma predictive interval (predictive_t-based) of the injected ground truth in >=90% of replicates (a calibration check, not just a point-estimate bias check) -- this is the honest-covariance discipline already used elsewhere in this repo (tyre_supplant zstd-style calibration). (b) SEPARABILITY -- the fit's own posterior/estimated covariance between the curve's initial value and each session's offset has correlation magnitude < 0.8 (named threshold, frozen before the real-data run) in >=90% of replicates; a correlation pinned near +-1 means the two parameters are aliased (indistinguishable from the data) even though the point estimates may look reasonable, which is exactly the failure T2/pre-ruling decision:synthetic-identifiability warns about. Falsified (per issue's own falsification clause) if either (a) or (b) fails at the stated replicate rate.

q6-artifact-shape.imperative: Resolve the concrete file layout for G's module following the estimate-store pattern (design-it-twice explicitly skipped per issue/spec -- precedented shape): new module under src/physics/layer2/ (e.g. grip_baseline.py or grip_store.py + grip_batch.py), a GripEstimateRecord dataclass (PK likely (year, gp_name, session_type) -- session-level, NOT per-constructor since G is field-pooled and shared across all cars), standalone SQLite store mirroring EstimateStore's has/upsert/load + additive-only migration, and a query surface every consumer calls to subtract G. q6-artifact-shape.finding: FACT resolved, grounded in estimate_store.py (lines 60-239, 400-412) and estimate_batch.py (full file): new module src/physics/layer2/grip_baseline.py (fit logic: intra-session saturating curve g(cumulative_track_laps) via a chosen saturating form e.g. asymptote*(1-exp(-rate*x)), Student-t residuals via student_t.predictive_t) + src/physics/layer2/grip_store.py (GripEstimateRecord dataclass + GripStore class, mirroring EstimateStore's shape) + src/physics/layer2/grip_batch.py (run_grip_batch, mirroring run_estimate_batch's injectable-fn batch driver). Fields: identity (year,gp_name,session_type,session_id), fit outputs (curve_asymptote,curve_asymptote_sigma,curve_rate,curve_rate_sigma,session_offset,session_offset_sigma,curve_offset_correlation [the T2 separability diagnostic]), fit-quality (n_stints_used,n_drivers_used,n_laps_used,fit_status ok|thin_fallback|error,fallback_reason), the reused cumulative_track_laps bridge convention, rain_flag, fitted_at. Standalone SQLite store (own .db, own connection, additive-only migration via the same PRAGMA table_info + ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN pattern at estimate_store.py:400-412), query surface has()/upsert()/load()/get_grip_at(...) (the consumer-facing subtract-G call). Tests mirror tests/unit/physics/layer2/test_estimate_store.py + test_estimate_batch.py -> test_grip_store.py + test_grip_batch.py.

q7-tyre-separation-peer.title: Confirm G does not silently duplicate or break tyre_separation.py's g_track
q7-tyre-separation-peer.imperative: tyre_separation.py's ratified g_track(gp, cumulative_track_laps) is a differently-scoped (race-stint grain, decay-separation purpose) peer implementation, per its own decision doc's Review Trigger: 'If pooling.py is extended to support within-session covariate axes, evaluate whether the two implementations should be unified.' Confirm G's Build-1 scope treats this as an explicitly out-of-scope peer to NOT touch/replace/import from (issue #663 doesn't mention it), record that as a triage candidate for a future reconciliation issue rather than doing it in this build, and confirm this reading against docs/architecture/decisions/tyre-age-g-track-design.md.
q7-tyre-separation-peer.finding: FACT confirmed via docs/architecture/decisions/tyre-age-g-track-design.md (decision:tyre_age_g_track_design, current): g_track(gp,cumulative_track_laps) is a PER-CIRCUIT LINEAR slope, DerSimonian-Laird tau-squared partial-pooled ACROSS SEASONS (race-side, race_stint_store, decay-separation nuisance term) -- structurally distinct from G (a per-WEEKEND, per-SESSION saturating curve + free session offsets, field-pooled within one weekend, general-purpose grip-baseline consumer surface). The doc's own Review Trigger only fires on new session_type values in race_stint_store or on pooling.py extension -- neither applies to G, which is a new standalone module, not a modification of tyre_separation.py or its store. Issue #663 does not name tyre_separation.py as in-scope. CONFIRMED: G's Build-1 scope treats tyre_separation.py/g_track as an untouched peer; a future reconciliation (per the doc's own Review Trigger reasoning, now that a second within-session-covariate implementation -- G -- exists) is filed as a triage candidate, not done in this build.
